questions.question: If Teacher’s Day was on Tuesday in 1995, what day will it be in 1996?
questions.solution:
In an ordinary year, there are 365 days and on dividing 365 by 7, we get remainder = 1 so this extra one day is taken as an odd day.

Similarly, in a leap year, there are 366 days and on dividing 366 by 7, we get remainder = 2 so these extra days are taken as the odd days.

Thus, the remainder, which we get after dividing a number of days by 7 is considered as odd days.

Now, we have to calculate the odd days from 5th September, 1995 to 5th September, 1996.

5th September, 1995 – 5th September, 1996 = 2 odd day i.e. 2 more day(as 1996 is leap year) after Tuesday.

Therefore, Teacher’s day in 1996 will fall on Thursday.

Hence, **‘Thursday’** is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a row of 48 students facing North, Tinu is 15th from the left end. If Dinesh is 9th to the right of Tinu, what is Dinesh's position from the right end of the line?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c2f9ff60afd1c6e4a177e6ef0e3cc4a38d0256dbaa9469faf24568ab4cc64c6.png] 

 

So, Dinesh's position from the right end of the line = 48 - (15 + 9) + 1 = 48 - 24 + 1 = **25**

questions.question: In a code language, if ‘PALACE’ is coded as ‘19’, then how will ‘FOREST’ be coded in the same language?
questions.solution:

Taking the sum of positional values and dividing by 2,

PALACE = 16 + 1 + 12 + 1 + 3 + 5 = 38 and 38 ÷ 2 = 19

Similarly,

FOREST = 6 + 15 + 18 + 5 + 19 + 20 = 83 and 83 ÷ 2 = 41.5

Hence, ’41.5’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Words given on the left side of (∶∶) are related with each other by some Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the missing word/word pair on the right side of (∶∶) from the given alternatives based on the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

Caterpillar ∶ Butterfly ∶∶ ?
questions.solution:
The relationship established in "Caterpillar : Butterfly" is "Young form : Mature form". A caterpillar is the immature form (larva) of a butterfly.

Following this logic, from the given options, a lamb is the young form of a sheep. Therefore, "Lamb : Sheep" follows the same relationship.

As for the other options:

 
• "Tadpole : Cat" is incorrect because a tadpole (young form of a frog or toad) does not mature into a cat.
 
• "Hen : Chick" and "Deer : Fawn" have the relationship reversed. A chick is a young hen and a fawn is a young deer, so they do not match the initial relationship pattern.

Hence,the correct answer is "**Lamb : Sheep".**
